newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Data vacuum sucks out Australian bond interest.
newsitem.headline: Data vacuum sucks out Australian bond interest.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained above their early lows during a slow moving morning session.
*Rate cut speculation expected to limit price pullbacks, although data vacuum proving a drain on market interest.
Australian bond yields remained above their initial lows during an extremely slow moving morning session, partially retracing the rally seen in after hours trading late on Friday.
Bonds futures had raced ahead in SYCOM supported by a rally in U.S. Treasuries, although traders said the move had been exaggerated in low turnover.
"Obviously, there was buying from the offshore, but not sufficient to justify the move we saw. But pull-backs from here will be limited as we await a possible rate cut," one trader said.

Rate cut speculation has been paramount in the market's thinking in the past couple of weeks, and futures contracts struck their low points for the day when once again the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy.

While the market will be on full alert at the RBA's 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) usual policy announcement time every day this week, an easing is seen as more logical after the July 1 RBA board and July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meetings.
In the meantime, turnovers are likely to be fairly shallow with the market again suffering from a lack of key data this week.

Spreads to the dollar bloc showed a mild narrowing bias despite the local market's pull-back from their early yield lows which again saw the benchmark October 2007 bond toying with 7.0 percent. New Zealand debt remained under pressure ahead of this Thursday's budget and Friday's RBNZ monetary policy statement.

The 10-year bond contract eased back from a SYCOM close of 93.000, but is finding support at around 92.950. Initial resistance is pegged at 93.015 before the market has another assault on last Monday's 3-1/4 year high of 93.090.
